key_insight: CCL alternates source-domain teacher calibration with target-domain student learning so the student can recover an oracle-like policy and reduce teacher bias without target reward feedback.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical distillation recipe for deploying smaller LLMs under distribution shift when target labels or rewards are unavailable.
method: Calibrate the teacher on source questions using reward feedback only.
Train the student on target questions with the calibrated teacher via token-level branching.
Iterate: use the updated student to improve the next calibration step in an autoregressive policy framework.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical convergence result: the student's expected average KL divergence to the oracle student goes to zero at a polynomial rate, and it also shows direct matching can remain error-bounded away from zero.
watch_item: The guarantee is theoretical and depends on iterative calibration, projected gradient updates, and an autoregressive policy setting, so performance may be sensitive to approximation error and optimization stability in practice.
paper_title: Coupled Calibration and Learning: Mitigating Teacher Bias in LLM Distillation without Target-Domain Reward Feedback
